Description: Wheat or meslin flour.
Exemptions: The ban will not be applicable to transitional arrangements nor in the case of permissions granted by Government of India to other countries to meet their food security needs and based on the request of their government.
Notes: Wheat flour had been excluded from the wheat export ban implemented in May 2022, but in view of the sudden increase in demand for wheat flour, on 27 August 2022, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry also banned exports of wheat or meslin flour. On the same date and in advance of the export prohibition, the Ministry through Notification No. 29/2015-2020 withdrew a provision that exempted exports of wheat or meslin flour from any restriction or ban. On 14 October 2022, India authorized export-oriented units and firms set up in Special Economic Zones to export flour made from imported wheat (Notification No. 39/2015-2020). This last notifcation was further amended in other notifications [On 25 November 2022, India allowed conditional re-export of wheat flour made from imported wheat (Notification No. 38/2015-2020). On 23 March 2023, India amended the wheat flour export condition that only multigrain/fortified wheat flour with at least 80% whole wheat flour will be permitted and that all other ingredients in the final product must be sourced locally (Notification No. 62/2015-2020). On 4 August 2023, India allowed conditional export of wheat flour mixed with millets (Notification No. 25/2023).]
Source: Government of India, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Directorate General of Foreign Trade

Notes: Variable export tax, calculated each week, based on formula shown in [Measure] field. On 1 June, the Government of the Russian Federation changed the base price for calculating the export duty for wheat from RUB 15 000 to RUB 17 000 per tonne of wheat.
Measure_Description: Ct = (Ce x Ckr -  Cb) * 0.7 if Ce < Cb2; Ct = (Ce - Cb2) * Ckr * 0.8 + (Cb2 x Ckr - Cb) * 0.7 if Cb2 <= Ce < Cb3; Ct = (Ce - Cb3 ) * Ckr * 0.9 + (Cb3 - Cb2 ) * Ckr * 0.8 + (Cb2 * Ckr - Cb ) * 0.7 if Ce >= Cb3, where: Ce - indicative price for 1 ton, Cb  - base export price, which has the following meaning: 17000 rubles, Cb2: 375 US dollars, Cb3: 400 US dollars - when calculating the export customs duty on wheat and meslin. Ckr - the arithmetic mean of the exchange rate of the US dollar against the ruble of the Russian Federation, established by the Central Bank of the Russian Federation, for 5 working days preceding the date of calculation of the export customs duty rate for grain crops. With a negative value of Ct obtained in the calculation in accordance with this paragraph, the value is assumed to be zero.
Source: Government of the Russian Federation
